key_insight: TRAMA transfers knowledge from a cheap linear property into a reusable learned search space for optimizing nonlinear mechanical metamaterial behavior.
engineering_relevance: More efficient energy-absorption optimization can reduce costly finite-element evaluations, saving approximately 100 hours per design campaign.
method: Reparametrize metamaterial architectures with a variational autoencoder.
Use a pre-trained vision transformer and physics-informed augmentations.
Transfer the learned representation to nonlinear, potentially non-differentiable design targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 95–98% fewer evaluations than state-of-the-art gradient-free optimization for energy-absorption efficiency targets, with fabricated designs matching simulated stress–strain curves within 5.3%.
watch_item: Transfer is property-dependent: the learned representation does not generalize equally well to every new target.
paper_title: Efficient Optimization of Mechanical Metamaterials via Transferable Representation Learning
